entries.title: a JavaScript method called through a string key is recorded as called
entries.summary: JavaScript and TypeScript reach a member by a string as well as a dot: `t["m"]()` calls what `t.m()` calls. The parser recorded the container `t` for it and nothing for the method, so a method called only that way read `no_callers` in `get_dead_code_v2`. A key that is a string holding a name is read as the name now. No function on the eight pinned repositories changes; the effect is on a method whose only call has this shape. A key that is a variable, a number or a string that is not a name still records the container; the CHANGELOG lists the limits. An existing index is re-parsed on upgrade.

entries.title: a Ruby method called by its bare name is recorded as called
entries.summary: Ruby writes a call of a method with no receiver and no arguments as a bare name (`settings`), and the parser recorded no call for it. A helper called only that way read `no_callers` in `get_dead_code_v2`. Each method is now read the way Ruby reads it: a bare name is a call unless the method has made a local variable of that name by then. On sinatra at a pinned commit the rows reported `no_callers` fall from 176 to 152 in the default call and none is newly reported. Code outside every method is still not read; the CHANGELOG lists that and the other limits. An existing index is re-parsed on upgrade.

entries.title: a Go generic function called with one argument is recorded as called
entries.summary: Go's grammar parses `Generic[int](1)`, a generic function called with exactly one argument, as a type conversion, and the parser recorded no call for it. A generic function called only that way could read `no_callers` in `get_dead_code_v2`. The call is recorded now, also behind `*` or in parentheses, and so is a function taken from a slice or map by a variable (`fs[i](1)`). On eight pinned repositories 24 functions gain a recorded call and no dead-code row moves; the effect is on a function whose only call has this shape. A real conversion to a generic type records the type's name; the CHANGELOG lists that limit. An existing index is re-parsed on upgrade.

entries.title: a C# constructor is no longer reported as having no caller when its class is created
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` reported a C# constructor with no caller however often its class was created, because `new Made(...)` recorded no call. It records `Made` now, for plain, generic, qualified and alias-qualified classes. On RestSharp the `no_callers` rows fall from 101 to 73 in the default call, every row that left is a constructor, and no row is newly reported. A target-typed `new()`, `: base(...)` and an attribute still record nothing; the CHANGELOG lists those and the other limits. An existing index is re-parsed on upgrade.
